Along the coast

The tide had already turned when we reached the harbour. On the water, a narrow line of morning light followed the boats out to sea.

From the pier, we could hear the bell of a buoy in the fog. The harbour wall kept the sheltered water still, even as waves broke outside.

A signal rose from the tower as the first ferry left the inlet. Its flag was bright against the sky, and it stayed raised until the bay was clear.

Weather notes. A light north wind carried the sound of gulls over the headland. By noon, the low cloud had cleared and the cliffs were visible again.
